verified_facts: GitHub Actions run 37741046518 failed at the Node.js execution step while running 'ChatMachines/GitHubNodeTest/run.js' calling JS Runner and 'metaprocedures/procedures/AchiveExtraction/procedure.json'.

The remote Apps Script endpoint (https://script.google.com/macros/s/AKfycbxz7tkba4wl-wWzDn90iuh0us2l2EUD3AYV9HyVJckETKGjhPKFthnqPyYmcOPOk_g5FA/exec) returned HTTP status 200 with an HTML document titled 'Error'.

The specific exception recorded in the Apps Script HTML body was: 'Exception: You do not have permission to call DriveApp.createFile. Required permissions: https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive' at line 12 of the server execution context.
No run-scoped report file for run_id 'archive_extraction_20261007_1' was generated or persisted in Google Drive.

In 'metaprocedures/procedures/AchiveExtraction/apps-script-source.js', line 12 corresponds to the helper function `createOutput`, specifically `DriveApp.createFile(blob)` (invoked when `input.destination.folder_id` is null).

At line 74 of `apps-script-source.js`, `createOutput` is called unconditionally to write the final JSON execution report to Google Drive (`const resultFile = createOutput(reportName, JSON.stringify(report,null,2), 'application/json');`).

In 'metaprocedures/procedures/AchiveExtraction/procedure.json', lines 38-42 of the client script enforce that the response body must start with '{' and parse as JSON containing `report_file_id` matching `config.run_id`. Because Apps Script returned HTML error markup, the client script threw: 'Apps Script returned non-JSON content; remote result cannot be verified'.

root_causes.description: The deployed Apps Script Web App executes under an identity or authorization scope that lacks write access (`https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive`). Web Apps configured to execute as 'User accessing the web app' or deployed without re-authorizing the project manifest (`appsscript.json`) containing `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive` throw runtime permission exceptions when attempting mutative Drive calls such as `DriveApp.createFile`.

`apps-script-source.js` unnecessarily requires `DriveApp.createFile` solely to write the execution report and return a file locator. Because the Apps Script `doPost` endpoint is an `eval(sourcecode)(arguments)` bridge returning directly to the HTTP transport caller, the execution report can be returned directly in the HTTP JSON response body via `ContentService.createTextOutput(JSON.stringify(report))`. Forcing report persistence to Drive creates a fragile dependency on broad Drive write permissions even for read-only actions like `inspect` and `list_entries`.

The client script in `procedure.json` expects an immediate JSON response carrying `report_file_id`, and does not handle structured HTTP 200 HTML error envelopes gracefully before asserting valid JSON, resulting in a generic non-JSON parse crash.

mistake_pattern: Conflating HTTP transport success (200 OK) with Apps Script execution success (Google Apps Script web apps return HTTP 200 with HTML error bodies when an unhandled server-side exception occurs).
Assuming the Apps Script execution identity has root Drive creation permissions (`DriveApp.createFile`) without explicit `folder_id` write permissions or explicit OAuth scope authorization.
Enforcing persistent Drive file creation for procedure metadata/reporting when ephemeral direct return over the HTTP bridge is supported by the runtime bridge.

repairs.action: Open the Google Apps Script project associated with deployment ID `AKfycbxz7tkba4wl-wWzDn90iuh0us2l2EUD3AYV9HyVJckETKGjhPKFthnqPyYmcOPOk_g5FA`. Ensure `appsscript.json` includes `oauthScopes: ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive"]`. In the Apps Script editor, run any dummy function invoking `DriveApp.createFile` to trigger the OAuth authorization consent flow. Redeploy the Web App (or update the active deployment) configured to 'Execute as: Me' and 'Who has access: Anyone'.

Modify `apps-script-source.js` to decouple the report output from mandatory `DriveApp.createFile`. Attempt `createOutput` inside a try/catch block for the report, but always embed the full `report` object in the function return payload. If `DriveApp.createFile` fails or is skipped, set `report_file_id: null` and return the complete JSON report directly.

In `procedure.json` script, update the verification condition: if the remote payload returns the full execution report directly in the JSON response, treat the dispatch and execution as verified even if `report_file_id` is null, or require `folder_id` with pre-granted folder permissions instead of root Drive creation.

verification_plan: Verify whether the Apps Script deployment permissions can be updated in the Google Apps Script project console.
If Apps Script permissions cannot be updated immediately, update `apps-script-source.js` to return the execution report directly in the return object rather than failing at line 12.
Test dispatch with `inspect` action on archive `1MxvFWzM9b-HnZlfr29kzmbqx5BbBetOK` to verify read permissions without requiring `DriveApp.createFile`.
Trigger `ChatMachines/GitHubNodeTest/run.js` via git push and assert that the diagnostic output confirms valid JSON receipt.
limitations: GitHub Actions and git commits cannot grant OAuth tokens or authorize OAuth scopes for Google Apps Script. Re-authorizing `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive` and updating the Web App deployment requires interactive authorization in the Google Cloud/Apps Script account owning the deployment.
If the Apps Script project was deployed with 'Execute as: User accessing the web app', anonymous POST calls from GitHub Actions will always fail authorization or prompt for sign-in HTML.
recommended_next_operation: Inspect and update the Apps Script project manifest to include 'https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive' and re-authorize the Web App deployment with 'Execute as: Me', while modifying 'apps-script-source.js' to return the report payload in the return object so execution does not unconditionally abort if Drive report creation fails.
